first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly threatening activation metrics. memory_31 demonstrated durable lift in first-week activation for SMB through field reduction, and memory_86 confirmed that shortening onboarding improves both completion and time-to-value. Both directly address the measured activation decline. I am verifying memory_31 to confirm the methodology and sustainability of the signup simplification effect, and memory_73 to evaluate whether promotional pricing alone would be sufficient—but the activation decline suggests a friction problem, not pure price sensitivity. Simplifying onboarding is lower-risk than promotional pricing (which could erode margin and invite further price competition) and more directly targeted than referral incentives (which address growth after activation, not the upstream drop). Enterprise sales assist is orthogonal to the SMB activation crisis. This preserves uncertainty about whether pricing contributes to the competitor threat while focusing on the measurable internal metric decline.
